subject: anatomy
title: Nerve lesions, veins and lymphatics of the lower limb

steps.tx: The **common peroneal nerve** is the smaller terminal branch of the sciatic nerve (L4 to S2). It winds around the neck of the fibula, so it is easily injured there by fracture, tight plaster or a lathi blow to the lateral knee. Its paralysis causes **foot drop**, loss of eversion and loss of toe extension, with a high stepping gait. Ankle jerk remains intact in this lesion.
steps.say: The common peroneal nerve is the smaller terminal branch of the sciatic nerve, arising from L4 to S2. It winds around the neck of the fibula, so it is easily injured there by fracture, tight plaster or a blow to the lateral knee. Its paralysis causes foot drop, loss of eversion and loss of toe extension, giving a high stepping gait. The ankle jerk remains intact in this lesion.

steps.tx: The **deep peroneal nerve** supplies the anterior compartment, so its injury abolishes dorsiflexion and causes foot drop. The **superficial peroneal nerve** supplies the evertors, peroneus longus and brevis. The sole is spared because it is supplied by the tibial nerve, through its medial and lateral plantar and calcaneal branches. Sensory loss from a peroneal lesion does not reach the sole.
steps.say: The deep peroneal nerve supplies the anterior compartment, so its injury abolishes dorsiflexion and causes foot drop. The superficial peroneal nerve supplies the evertors, peroneus longus and peroneus brevis. The sole is spared because it is supplied by the tibial nerve through its medial and lateral plantar and calcaneal branches.

steps.tx: **Tibial nerve** injury paralyses the posterior compartment, so the foot is dorsiflexed and everted, giving calcaneovalgus, and the sole loses sensation. **Femoral nerve** palsy weakens knee extension and the knee jerk. **Meralgia paraesthetica** is compression of the **lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh**, causing burning pain on the outer thigh worse on standing and walking. It is relieved by sitting and is common in obesity and pregnancy.
steps.say: Tibial nerve injury paralyses the posterior compartment, so the foot is dorsiflexed and everted, giving calcaneovalgus, and the sole loses sensation. Femoral nerve palsy weakens knee extension. Meralgia paraesthetica is compression of the lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh, causing burning pain on the outer thigh that worsens on standing and walking and eases on sitting. It is common in obesity and pregnancy.

steps.tx: The **great saphenous vein** starts at the medial end of the dorsal venous arch, runs 2.5 cm in front of the medial malleolus and drains into the femoral vein at the **saphenous opening**. The **small saphenous vein** runs behind the lateral malleolus with the sural nerve and ends in the popliteal vein. **Perforators** connect superficial to deep veins and their valves allow flow only from superficial to deep. Incompetent valves cause varicose veins.
steps.say: The great saphenous vein starts at the medial end of the dorsal venous arch, runs two and a half centimetres in front of the medial malleolus and drains into the femoral vein at the saphenous opening. The small saphenous vein runs behind the lateral malleolus with the sural nerve and ends in the popliteal vein. Perforators connect superficial to deep veins, and their valves allow flow only outward from superficial to deep. Incompetent valves cause varicose veins.

steps.tx: A **Trendelenburg test** checks valve competence in the saphenofemoral junction. The limb is elevated to empty the veins, a tourniquet is applied high on the thigh, and the patient stands. Rapid refilling of the varicose veins indicates incompetent saphenofemoral valves. The superficial inguinal nodes drain the scrotum, penis, buttocks and lower anal canal. Below the pectineal line, the lymph drains to the **superficial inguinal nodes**.
steps.say: A Trendelenburg test checks valve competence at the saphenofemoral junction. The limb is elevated to empty the veins, a tourniquet is applied high on the thigh, and the patient stands. Rapid refilling of the varicose veins suggests incompetent saphenofemoral valves. Below the pectineal line, lymph drains to the superficial inguinal nodes, which also receive lymph from the scrotum, penis and buttocks.

steps.tx: The **sural nerve** runs with the small saphenous vein and supplies the back of the lower leg and the lateral foot. Its injury, for example during harvesting of the lesser saphenous vein for grafting, causes lateral leg and foot numbness without foot drop. The great saphenous vein is the usual bypass conduit for coronary, femoral or brachial artery surgery and is reversed so its valves do not obstruct arterial flow.
steps.say: The sural nerve runs with the small saphenous vein and supplies the back of the lower leg and the lateral foot. Its injury, for example during harvesting of the lesser saphenous vein for grafting, causes numbness of the lateral leg and foot without foot drop. The great saphenous vein is the usual bypass conduit and is reversed so its valves do not obstruct arterial flow.
